source: Gemini (BYOK), AI-interpreted multilingual meanings and pedagogical usage notes. 28 Aug 2026: regenerated grounded in real source text where available (85% of roots) -- this repo's own integrated vritti/ (Madhaviya Dhatuvritti, Kshiratarangini, Dhatupradipa; samsaadhanii/scl, GPL-2.0) plus a local build of bhumandala-kosha-data's dictionary corpus (same three vrittis in headword-keyed form, plus Monier-Williams/Macdonell/Capeller/Apte, mostly CC-BY-SA 4.0 via indic-dict/stardict-sanskrit -- some entries in that corpus carry an unclear licence, used per the project lead's explicit direction). Each item's own `sources_used` records what real text was actually fed in for that root; absent/empty means no match was found and the entry falls back to Gemini's general knowledge, not a false attribution. The remaining 15% with no `sources_used` are Gemini's own interpretation, same as before. See tools/gemini_dhatu_lexicon.py and tools/dhatu_grounding.py.
licence: AI-interpreted; grounded in real source text where sources_used is present, AI-generated general knowledge otherwise -- see per-item sources_used

meanings.English: To be, to become, to exist, to happen
meanings.Hindi: hona, vidyaman hona, utpann hona, ghatit hona

pedagogy.concept: The root BU primarily means 'to be' or 'to become' in the active voice (parasmaipada). However, when taking specific suffixes, prefixes, or entering the passive or impersonal (bhāva) constructions, its sense can shift to denote states of mutual action, inherent qualities, or impersonal occurrences.

scenarios.meaning: To be, to become, or to exist
scenarios.example_english: A son who desires prosperity comes into being.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: lat (present tense), ātmanepada in impersonal passive (bhāva) sense
scenarios.example_english: It is being by Chaitra (Chaitra exists/acts impersonally).

scenarios.meaning: To perform mutual or reciprocal actions of being/becoming
scenarios.example_english: He reciprocates by engaging in another's intended process of becoming.

meanings.English: To grow, to increase, to thrive, to prosper
meanings.Hindi: baṛhnā, vṛddhi honā, panapnā, vikasit honā
meanings.Chinese: sheng zhang, zeng zhang, fan rong, fa da

pedagogy.concept: The root eḍh inherently means growth or prosperity and canonically takes ātmanepada endings (e.g., edhate). When modified into the causative form via the ṇic suffix, it expresses causing something else to grow or thrive, as seen in the Mādhavīya Dhātuvṛtti.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (ṇic suffix) with a sentient subject (citvatkartṛka) in certain contexts
scenarios.example_english: He makes the son grow / nourishes the son.

meanings.English: To vie, to compete, to emulate, to struggle
meanings.Kannada: spardhisu, s स्पर्धा madu, potti madu
meanings.Tamil: potti idu, poramai kol, muyandru vel
meanings.Hindi: spardha karna, mukabla karna, sangharsh karna

pedagogy.concept: The root spardh- primarily expresses rivalry or competition (saṅgharṣe) and natively takes Ātmanepada endings. Through grammatical additions like the causative (ṇic), it can take Parasmipada endings when expressing the instigation of competition.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (ṇic) with present tense (Laṭ), 3rd person singular, Parasmipada
scenarios.meaning: To cause to compete or incite rivalry

meanings.English: To establish, to desire to obtain, to bind in a text

pedagogy.concept: The root gādhṛँ expresses three core ideas per traditional authorities: establishing (pratiṣṭhā), desiring to obtain (lipsā), and composing or stringing together a text (grantha). Depending on the specific sense and usage, it shifts between intransitive and transitive behaviours, and can form standard desiderative (sananta) and causative (ṇijanta) derivatives.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Ātmanepada present indicative (laṭ), root sense of grounding or resting
scenarios.meaning: To establish oneself or be firmly situated

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Desiderative (sananta) form indicating the desire to obtain (lipsā)
scenarios.meaning: To desire to obtain or establish

meanings.English: To oppress, to harass, to afflict, to obstruct
meanings.Bengali: kashta deoya, badha deoya, pidan kara

pedagogy.concept: The root bādh (bhvādi-gaṇa, ātmanepada) primarily means to oppress, harass, or obstruct (loḍana / roṭana). As an ātmanepada root, its forms reflect affliction or resistance directed towards an object.

meanings.English: To beg, to afflict, to rule, to bless
meanings.Hindi: Bhikh mangana, kashta dena, rajya karna, ashirvad dena
meanings.Bengali: Prarthana kara, kashta dewa, aishvarya, ashirbad

pedagogy.concept: The root nādh takes Ātmanepada specifically when expressing a blessing (āśiḥ), requiring the genitive case for the object of desire. In other senses like begging or troubling, it takes Parasmaipada.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Ātmanepada in the sense of a blessing (āśiḥ)
scenarios.meaning: To pray for or bless with something (with genitive)
scenarios.example_english: He prays for clarified butter (as a blessing).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Parasmaipada outside the sense of a blessing

meanings.English: To beg, to ask, to afflict, to rule, to bless
meanings.Hindi: yaचना करना, माँगना, कष्ट देना, शासन करना, आशीर्वाद देना
meanings.Bengali: yācñā karā, chāoẏā, kaṣṭa deẏā, śāsana karā, āśīrbāda karā

pedagogy.concept: The root nātṛ (nath) primarily expresses four semantic fields: begging or asking (yācñā), affliction or torment (upatāpa), exercising lordship or supremacy (aiśvarya), and blessing or invoking good wishes (āśīṣ).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ laṅkāra (Present tense), 3rd person singular, Ātmanepada

meanings.English: To hold, to bear, to possess, to maintain

pedagogy.concept: The root daDa~ means 'to hold or maintain' (dhārane) and exclusively takes Ātmanepada endings in its primary conjugation. It also forms intensive (yaṅanta) derivations expressing intensity or repetition of holding.

scenarios.example_sanskrit: tadvēṣosadṛśonyābhistrībhirmadhuratābhṛtaḥ dadhate sulabhāṁ śobhāṁ tadīyā vibhramā iva
scenarios.example_english: Resembling that hatred, filled with sweetness by other women, they bear an easy beauty like their sports.

meanings.English: To leap, to spring up, to bound, to jump

pedagogy.concept: The root skudi~ (class 1 ātmanepada) means to leap, spring up, or bound (āpravana). Because it is an nasal-incremented root (itit), it takes the num augment, transforming forms like skundate. It also admits intensive (yaṅanta) and causative formations as detailed in traditional commentaries.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ laṅkāra (Present tense), 3rd person singular, ātmanepada

scenarios.meaning: He causes to leap or bound

meanings.English: To be white, to become white, to show whiteness
meanings.Hindi: safed hona, safed dikhai dena, shvetata

pedagogy.concept: The root Svidi~ specifically denotes the quality of whiteness (shvaitya) treated as an action or process. Per the Madhaviya Dhatuv vritti and Ksiratarangini, even though whiteness is normally a static quality, the verb presents it as a dynamic process coming to manifestation (as seen in the form shvindate).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Atmanepada present tense (lat), with nasal augmentation (num-agama) per traditional grammarians
scenarios.meaning: It is becoming white / manifesting whiteness
scenarios.example_english: The palace is becoming white (per Ksiratarangini)

meanings.English: To salute, to greet, to praise, to worship
meanings.Hindi: namaskar karna, vandana karna, stuti karna, puja karna
meanings.Bengali: namaskar kara, bandana kara, stuti kara, puja kara
meanings.Chinese: wen hou, li bai, zan mei, jing jing

pedagogy.concept: The root vadi~ (commonly appearing as vande in usage) belongs to the first gaṇa and is primarily ātmanepada, expressing the dual meanings of respectful salutation (abhivādana) and praise or worship (stuti).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Addition of the āru pratyaya expressing habitual agent (tacchīla)
scenarios.meaning: One who habitually bows or praises

meanings.English: To be auspicious, to rejoice, to be happy, to bless
meanings.Hindi: Kalyan hona, sukh pana, prasanna hona
meanings.Bengali: Kalyan houa, sukhi houa, anandita houa
meanings.French: Être propice, être heureux, se réjouir
meanings.Chinese: 吉祥, 幸福, 欢喜

pedagogy.concept: The root Badi~ strictly takes Atmanepada and primarily expresses the states of auspiciousness, well-being, or happiness. In the causative (curādi gaṇa), it shifts to denote the action of shaving or tonsuring (parivāpana).

scenarios.meaning: To be happy or to experience well-being
To shave or tonsure (per Mādhavīya Dhātuvṛtti)

meanings.English: To praise, to rejoice, to be intoxicated or proud, to sleep, to shine, to move
meanings.Hindi: stuti karna, prasanna hona, garv karna, sona, chalna
meanings.Bengali: stuti kara, ananda kara, garva kara, ghumano, chala
meanings.German: loben, sich freuen, stolz sein, schlafen, glänzen, sich bewegen
meanings.French: louer, se réjouir, être enivré, dormir, briller, se mouvoir
meanings.Russian: khvalit', radovat'sya, gordit'sya, spat', siyat', dvigat'sya
meanings.Chinese: zansong, xiyue, jiaoao, shuiyan, guanghui, yundong

pedagogy.concept: The root madi~ spans several distinct semantic domains according to traditional commentaries like the Mādhavīya Dhātuvṛtti and Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī, including praise (stuti), joy/rejoicing (moda), pride or intoxication (mada), sleep or sluggishness (svapna), beauty/lustre (kānti), and motion (gati). It is conjugated in Ātmanepada.

scenarios.meaning: He praises, rejoices, or displays sluggishness
scenarios.example_english: He rejoices or acts sluggishly per the root's senses.

meanings.English: To quiver, to throb, to tremble, to move slightly

pedagogy.concept: The root spadi~ primarily means slight movement or quivering (kiñcillane). As an Ātmanepada root in the bhvādi-gaṇa, it forms intransitive verbs like spandate. When the causal suffix (ṇic) is added, it shifts to Parasmaipada as noted in the Mādhavīya Dhātuvṛtti.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (ṇic) base with Parasmaipada ending per the rule 'nigaraṇacalanārthebhyaśca'

meanings.English: To lament, to bewail, to grieve
meanings.Chinese: bei shang, ku qi, dan you

pedagogy.concept: The root klidi~ primarily means to lament or grieve (paridevana). While it appears in traditional listings under different markers to explain pada distribution for agent-oriented or non-agent-oriented results, the standard forms illustrate its core action of sorrow.

meanings.English: To rejoice, to be glad, to take delight, to be pleased
meanings.Hindi: khush hona, prasanna hona, aanandit hona
meanings.Bengali: ananda kora, khushi howa, hharsha kora
meanings.German: sich freuen, froh sein, glücklich sein
meanings.French: se réjouir, être joyeux, prendre plaisir

pedagogy.concept: The root muda~ belongs to the first gaṇa and is exclusively ātmanepada, expressing the inner state of joy, gladness, or taking delight. When modified into the causative form, it means to cause someone else to rejoice or to gladden them.

scenarios.meaning: He causes to rejoice or gladdens

meanings.English: To give, to offer, to bestow

pedagogy.concept: The root dada~ belongs to the first gaṇa and takes Ātmanepada endings exclusively, with its core meaning rooted in giving or relinquishing ownership of something for another's benefit per the Mādhavīya Dhātuvṛtti.

scenarios.example_english: They forcibly grant/give to the wise person (per Dhātupradīpa).

meanings.English: To taste, to relish, to experience, to find pleasant
meanings.Hindi: chakhna, swad lena, anubhav karna, ruchi rakhna
meanings.Bengali: swad neoya, aswadan kara, anubhav kara
meanings.Chinese: chang, pin wei, xiang shou, gan dao

pedagogy.concept: The root zvada~ fundamentally means to taste or to relish. When used in the sense of pleasing or tasting good (ruci), it takes a dative case for the one who is pleased, as seen in traditional commentaries.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Atmanepada present tense (lat), intransitive usage expressing 'giving pleasure/taste to'
scenarios.meaning: To be tasty or pleasing to someone
scenarios.example_english: The curds are pleasing to Devadatta (per the Mādhavīya Dhātuvṛtti).

meanings.English: To taste, to relish, to take pleasure in

pedagogy.concept: The root svarda- strictly belongs to the ātmanepada and primarily conveys the physical or mental act of tasting and relishing.

meanings.English: To respect, to play, to taste
meanings.Bengali: Samman kara, khela kara, swadite kara

pedagogy.concept: The root urda~ primarily conveys three distinct senses per traditional authorities: honoring or measuring (māna), playful activity (krīḍā), and tasting or enjoying (āsvādana). It typically takes ātmanepada endings.

scenarios.example_english: He shows respect, plays, or tastes.

scenarios.meaning: He has respected, played, or tasted
scenarios.example_english: He has shown respect, played, or tasted.

scenarios.meaning: He causes to respect, play, or taste
scenarios.example_english: He causes someone to show respect, play, or taste.

meanings.English: To play, to leap, to bound, to sport

pedagogy.concept: The root kurda~ fundamentally means to play or sport (krīḍāyām eva), and as an Ātmanepada verb, it expresses actions centered on the agent such as leaping or playing. Per traditional authorities, the restrictive particle 'eva' in its definition also hints that it may occasionally take on extended senses.

scenarios.example_english: He leaps, has leaped, will leap (per Mādhavīya Dhātuvṛtti).

meanings.English: To play, to sport, to frolic

pedagogy.concept: The root Kurda (to play or sport) is primarily an Atmanepada verb belonging to the first gaṇa. It expresses actions related to playfulness, sport, and joyous movement.

scenarios.example_english: The child plays in the water.

meanings.English: To play, to sport, to leap, to bound
meanings.Bengali: Khela kara, lafano, kudra, laf deya

pedagogy.concept: The root gurda~ belongs to the first gaṇa and is primarily used in ātmanepada, expressing the sense of play and sport, which connects to related movement forms such as leaping and bounding.

meanings.English: To play, to sport, to amuse

pedagogy.concept: The root guda~ is classified under the first conjugation and takes ātmanepada endings with the specific traditional meaning of sport or play (kriḍāyām).

meanings.English: To flow, to dissolve, to destroy, to cook
meanings.Hindi: bahana, nashta karana, hiṃsa karana, pakana
meanings.Bengali: kharaṇa kara, bināśa kara, hiṃsā kara, rānnā kara
meanings.Chinese: liu chu, xie lou, xiao mie, zhu fan

pedagogy.concept: The root sūda has a base sense of flowing or oozing (kṣaraṇa), which extends to expulsion, destruction, or rendering soft and tasty, and it can also take a causative form to mean preparing or processing something.

scenarios.example_english: May the Maruts destroy or sweeten the imperfect part.
The slaughterer prepares/refines the oblation with fire.

meanings.English: To sound indistinctly, to make an inarticulate sound, to resound, to roar
meanings.Kannada: aspashtavāgi śabda māḍu, dhvani māḍu, guṅgu
meanings.Chinese: fa chu mo hu de sheng yin, ming xiang

pedagogy.concept: The root hrād (hrAda~) belongs to the first gaṇa, takes ātmanepada endings, and primarily denotes making an indistinct or inarticulate sound, such as the rumbling of a drum or the faint sound of anklets as noted by Kṣīrasvāmin.

meanings.English: To utter an indistinct sound, to experience joy, to be glad
meanings.Kannada: aspashta shabdha madu, sukha padu, anandisu
meanings.Telugu: avyakta sabdamu cheyu, sukhamu pondu, santoshinchu
meanings.Hindi: avyakta shabd karna, sukh pana, prasanna hona
meanings.Bengali: avyakta sabda kara, sukha pawa, ananda kara
meanings.German: ein unklares Geräusch machen, sich freuen, glücklich sein
meanings.French: faire un son indistinct, éprouver de la joie, se réjouir
meanings.Russian: izdat' nerazborchivyy zvuk, ispytyvat' radost', radovat'sya
meanings.Chinese: fa chu bu mingxian de shengyin, ganshou kuaile, gaoxing

pedagogy.concept: The root hlādī~ primarily denotes making an inarticulate or low murmur and experiencing happiness or joy. It takes ātmanepada endings and undergoes specific root vowel shortenings in past participles (niṣṭhā) as noted by traditional authorities.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ laṅkāra (Present tense), 3rd person singular, Ātmanepada
scenarios.meaning: He rejoices or makes a low joyous sound

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Niṣṭhā (Past passive participle) with prefix pra, featuring upadhā-hrasva and nasal mutation per Mādhavīya Dhātuvṛtti

meanings.English: To taste, to relish, to enjoy, to savor

pedagogy.concept: The root svād- belongs to the first conjugation (bhvādi-gaṇa) and takes ātmanepada endings in its primary intransitive or reflexive sense of tasting or relishing. Through the addition of grammatical affixes, it forms causative and desiderative stems to express making someone taste or desiring to taste.

scenarios.meaning: Tastes, relishes, or enjoys the flavor.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Desiderative stem (sannanta) formed from the root

meanings.English: To emit flatulence, to make a despised sound, to break wind
meanings.Kannada: gudada sabda madu, nishsabda adhovata madu
meanings.German: furzen, einen unanständigen Laut von sich geben
meanings.Chinese: fangpi, fa chu bu hao de sheng yin

pedagogy.concept: The root parda~ belongs to the first gaṇa and takes ātmanepada endings exclusively, denoting the specific action of emitting an offensive or despised bodily sound (flatulence/guda-rava) as detailed in traditional commentaries.

scenarios.meaning: He/she emits a despised bodily sound (breaks wind)
scenarios.example_english: He makes a sound in the belly, he breaks wind (per the Mādhavīya Dhātuvṛtti).

meanings.English: To strive, to exert oneself, to attempt, to endeavor
meanings.Hindi: prayatna karana, koshisha karana, srama karana
meanings.Bengali: cheshta kara, prayatna kara, udyoga kara

pedagogy.concept: The root yatI~ belongs to the first gaṇa and is exclusively ātmanepada, carrying the core meaning of exertion or striving (prayatna). When combined with affixes or preverbs, it forms various nominal and verbal derivatives like yatna, āyatta, and the causative yātayati.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Addition of the prefix ā- and the niṣṭhā suffix -ta (with iḍ-abhāva due to īdit- status per Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī)
Application of the naṅ suffix denoting bhāva

meanings.English: To shine, to be bright

pedagogy.concept: The root yutf (bhāsane) belongs to the first conjugation (bhvādi-gaṇa) and takes ātmanepada endings. Its core sense revolves around shining or appearing bright, and it forms intensive and causative derivations as seen in traditional commentaries.

meanings.English: To shine, to be bright, to appear
meanings.Bengali: Aloha paoya, prakash paoya, dekha deya

pedagogy.concept: The root jutf~ belongs to the first conjugation (bhvādi-gaṇa) and is strictly Ātmanepada, carrying the core meaning of shining or appearing.

meanings.English: To beg, to ask, to request

pedagogy.concept: The root viTf~ belongs to the first conjugation (bhvādi-gaṇa) and is exclusively ātmanepada, carrying the primary sense of begging or asking (yācana). As a dvikarmaka root, it can take two objects per traditional authorities.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ la-kāra (Present tense), 3rd person singular, ātmanepada
scenarios.example_english: The old man begs for wealth.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Luṅ la-kāra (Aorist tense), 3rd person singular with augment a-

meanings.English: To beg, to ask, to entreat, to request
meanings.Hindi: bikh mangana, yachana karna, prarthana karna
meanings.Bengali: prarthana kara, bhiksha kara, yachana kara

pedagogy.concept: The root veTf~ belongs to the first conjugation (bhvādi-gaṇa) and is exclusively ātmanepada, carrying the core meaning of asking, begging, or supplicating (yācanā).

meanings.English: To be loose, to become slack, to relax, to loosen
meanings.Hindi: shithil hona, dheela hona, baandhna kholna, vichalit hona
meanings.Bengali: shithil hona, dhila hona, alada hona
meanings.Chinese: shi fang, song chi, xu ruo

pedagogy.concept: The root SraTi~ belongs to the first gaṇa, takes ātmanepada endings, and carries the core meaning of looseness or slackness (śaithilya). It can take prefixes or suffixes to form nouns and causative verbs expressing the act of loosening or weakening.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (ṇic) suffix added to the root
scenarios.meaning: To cause to loosen or slacken

meanings.English: To be crooked, to weave, to bind, to twist

pedagogy.concept: The root graTi~ fundamentally means to be crooked or to bind. In forms expressing passive or reflexive action (karma-kartari), suffixes like yak and ciṇ do not occur, showing special grammatical constraints.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Ātmanepada present tense in the sense of karma-kartari

meanings.English: To praise, to boast, to flatter
meanings.Hindi: prashansa karna, badai karna, shlagha karna

pedagogy.concept: The root katTa~ belongs to the first conjugation and takes ātmanepada endings. Its core meaning is ślāghā, which traditional commentators like Kṣīrasvāmin define as attributing qualities (guṇāropa), generally manifesting as praising, boasting, or flattering.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Derived with the suffix ḍhinuṇ per Pāṇini 3.2.153
scenarios.meaning: One who habitually boasts or speaks boastfully

meanings.English: To go continuously, to move constantly, to proceed steadily
meanings.German: fortwährend gehen, sich ständig bewegen, ununterbrochen wandern
meanings.French: aller continuellement, se déplacer sans cesse, marcher continuellement

pedagogy.concept: The root ata~ means continuous or constant motion (sātatyam gamane). As a typical intransitive verb of motion in the first gaṇa (parasmaipada), it forms standard active tenses and can take causative forms where the underlying agent becomes the object.

scenarios.meaning: He/she/it goes continuously or constantly moves.
scenarios.example_english: He goes to the village continuously.

scenarios.meaning: He/she/it will move constantly in the future.
To wish to go continuously or to move about repeatedly.
scenarios.example_english: He wishes to go on moving continuously.

meanings.English: To perceive, to understand, to know, to be conscious
meanings.Chinese: shi, zhi dao, gan wu, jue zhi

pedagogy.concept: The root citI~ primarily means perception, consciousness, or knowing (saṁjñāna). In the causative form, it shifts to making someone perceive or cause to know.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Addition of the ṇic suffix to denote causing action, taking an uninflected or double object per the Mādhavīya Dhātuvṛtti.
scenarios.meaning: To cause to perceive or inform

meanings.English: To sprinkle, to moisten, to drip, to shed
meanings.Chinese: Jiao shui, shi run, di luo

pedagogy.concept: The root cyuti~r belongs to the first conjugation (bhvādi-gaṇa) and primarily means to sprinkle or make moist (āsecana / ārdrībhāvana). Per the Mādhavīya Dhātuvṛtti, it can take optional markers in aorist forms and exhibits standard causative and desiderative patterns.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Aorist tense (luṅ) with optional aṅ-adesh per the rule 'irito vā'

meanings.English: To drop, to distill, to trickle, to sprinkle

pedagogy.concept: The root Scuti~r primarily means sprinkling or trickling (āsecana). Its derivatives reflect the action of liquids dropping or being poured.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Addition of the causative suffix nic
scenarios.meaning: To cause to drop or to cause to sprinkle

meanings.English: To trickle, to drop, to ooze, to flow

pedagogy.concept: The root scyuti~r (class 1, parasmaipada) primarily means to trickle, drop, or flow. Depending on morphological contexts such as prefixes or derived conjugations like the causative, the form exhibits phonological shifts involving s-palatalization and conjunct consonant simplifications as detailed in traditional commentaries.

meanings.English: To shine, to be bright

pedagogy.concept: The root jyutf~ belongs to the first conjugation (bhvādi-gaṇa) and is parasmaipada. Its primary sense revolves around shining or giving off light (bhāsana).

meanings.English: To churn, to agitate, to injure, to kill
meanings.Hindi: Matna, mathna, hinsaa karna, nAS karna
meanings.Chinese: Jiao ban, sha hai, cui hui

pedagogy.concept: The root maTi~ primarily carries dual senses of physical churning or agitating (such as churning curds) and aggressive harming or destroying. In its common derived forms, it extends to agents of destruction or completed states like churned substances.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Addition of the past passive participle suffix -ta to the root

meanings.English: To injure, to hurt, to distress, to torment
meanings.Hindi: hiṃsā karanā, dukh denā, saṅkleś karanā
meanings.Bengali: hiṃsā karā, duḥkha deoyā, pīḍā karā
meanings.Chinese: 伤害, 折磨, 痛苦

pedagogy.concept: The root kuTi~ primarily expresses two related notions: harming or injuring (hiṃsā) and distressing or troubling (saṅkleśa). Per the traditional commentaries, it operates in the first gaṇa as a parasmaipada root.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Bhavādi-gaṇa, laṭ-lakāra (present tense), prathama-puruṣa (third person) ekavacana (singular)
